findings.summary: A search across the local document corpora (DOJ Vol 11, Duggan, LMSBAND, Unified, Epstein 20K) found no direct mentions of Republic National Bank of New York or Republic New York Corporation in Epstein's banking records, wire transfers, or correspondence; every 'Republic National Bank' phrase match was a false positive. There is no evidence of an Epstein banking relationship with RNB. The connection runs instead through the Safra family: Jacqui Safra was a direct Epstein social associate.

Republic National Bank and the wider Safra empire sit at the intersection of intelligence-adjacent finance, organized-crime exposure, and the Epstein network, across several converging threads. On Iran-Contra, both RNB (NY) and Trade Development Bank (Geneva) served as conduits for Enterprise funds: RNB officer Nan Morabia delivered $150K cash to Adnan Khashoggi, and TDB held Enterprise funds in the 'Codelis' account (Walsh Report). On Russian organized crime, RNB exposed the roughly $10B Bank of New York / Mogilevich money-laundering pipeline (August 1998), while Safra had co-founded Hermitage Capital with Bill Browder (1996, $25M RNB seed). The death timeline is notable: Safra died in an arson fire on December 3, 1999, between RNB's Mogilevich exposure and the HSBC acquisition closing on December 31, 1999; the nurse Ted Maher, who had a Green Beret background, was convicted. The Epstein link runs through nephew Jacqui Safra — Edge Foundation dinners with Epstein, Bezos, and Gates (2012-14); a Jerusalem property offered first to Ronald Lauder (Mega Group) then to Epstein; and bank-loan difficulties floated as a financial opportunity. The Safra banks served as both conduit and victim in the Madoff fraud. Roughly 70 Safra entities appear in ICIJ offshore leaks, and the entire offshore infrastructure was absorbed by HSBC in 1999. Ron Soffer worked at RNB from 1988 to 1991, bridging the Safra world to the Epstein legal network, and Peter A. Cohen has been identified as a bridge between the Safra empire and Wall Street. No RNB documents appear in Epstein's 331K-page DOJ corpus — the connection runs through the family social network, not institutional banking.
RNB handled many Enterprise wire transfers per Walsh Report AND later adopted exemplary KYC policies per 2001 Levin PSI report (before HSBC acquisition)
findings.detail: Two contrasting references frame the bank's posture. The Walsh Report (p.221 fn.20) records that RNB 'handled many of the Enterprise's wire transfers' for Iran-Contra, meaning the bank processed covert financial flows for a secret US government operation involving illegal arms sales and contra funding. The Levin PSI Correspondent Banking Report (2001, p.30) cited Republic National Bank of New York (by then HSBC USA) as a 'notable exception' for the 'Know Your Customer Policy Statement' adopted for its International Banking Group, effective Dec 31, 1998 — a policy that may have been adopted because of lessons from the Iran-Contra and forfeiture experience. Edmond Safra founded RNB and also controlled Trade Development Bank in Geneva, where the Codelis account was held.

findings.summary: RNB handled Enterprise wire transfers AND had an officer coordinating off-book cash deliveries
findings.detail: Republic National Bank of New York (founded by Edmond Safra 1966, 452 Fifth Avenue) played a dual role in Iran-Contra: (1) It handled many of the Enterprise's legitimate wire transfers as a banking institution, and (2) one of its officers (Nan Morabia) coordinated an off-the-books cash delivery operation outside bank channels. Per the Walsh Report, Morabia stated the cash-delivery operation was conducted by her outside bank channels. RNB's institutional role in wire transfers was therefore separate from the Morabia family's personal cash operation, though the two were connected through Zucker's coordination. RNB was later acquired by HSBC in 1999 for $10.3B. Key RNB personnel per LittleSis: Edmond J. Safra (Founder 1966), Ezra Safra (employee), Jeffrey C. Keil (Vice Chairman 1984-1996), Theodore W. Kheel (Chairman 1966-1975), Meade H. Esposito (VP). RNB also had offshore entities in Guernsey and Panama.

findings.summary: RNB was America's largest gold bullion dealer -- critical context for Iran-Contra cash operations
findings.detail: Republic National Bank was the first American bank licensed to sell gold for industrial purposes. After the 1974 lifting of the private gold ownership ban, RNB became the nation's leading importer of gold coins and a major gold bullion dealer. This precious-metals background frames the Iran-Contra cash operations in several ways. The Safra family began as precious-metals traders in Ottoman Aleppo, Syria, and RNB's gold trading made it expert in physical cash and commodity handling. An officer at America's largest gold bank facilitating six-figure cash deliveries points to institutional competence in physical asset transfers, and the bank's culture of physical precious-metals trading may have normalized the handling of large amounts of physical cash. RNB was the 11th largest bank in the US.

curation.lead:
Republic National Bank of New York (RNB) was the American institutional anchor of the Edmond Safra banking empire, founded by Safra in 1966 at 452 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan and grown into one of the largest privately controlled banks in the United States. Its parent holding company, Republic New York Corporation, at peak held over $50 billion in assets [Finding #3414]. The bank operated in tandem with Safra's offshore architecture through Trade Development Bank in Geneva, Safra Republic Holdings in Luxembourg, and branches in Monaco, Guernsey, Singapore, and the Bahamas [Finding #3414]. RNB's FARA registration from 1975 to 1976 as agent for Trade Development Bank Overseas Inc. documents the institutional interdependence between the New York and Geneva operations at the primary-source level [FARA:2604].

The bank's record intersects several areas of public concern. In the Walsh Independent Counsel's Iran-Contra Final Report, RNB handled many of the Enterprise's wire transfers through normal banking channels while bank officer Nan Morabia ran a parallel off-books cash operation outside those channels, delivering funds to Enterprise participants including Adnan Khashoggi [Finding #3414][Finding #3390]. In the Bank of New York / Benex investigation, RNB's compliance team flagged the roughly $10 billion Russian money-laundering pipeline and filed Suspicious Activity Reports with the FBI in August 1998, months before Safra's death in a Monaco fire on December 3, 1999. The HSBC acquisition closed on December 31, 1999, transferring the Safra private banking network for $9.85 billion. Read together, the Walsh record and the 2001 Levin PSI Correspondent Banking Report show RNB occupying a dual posture, serving as a conduit for covert flows in the 1980s and as a model-compliance KYC adopter by the late 1990s [Finding #3390].

The connection to the Epstein investigation is structural rather than direct. A search of local document corpora — the DOJ Volume 11 corpus, Duggan, LMSBAND, Unified, and Epstein 20K datasets — found zero direct mentions of RNB in Epstein's banking records, wire transfers, or correspondence [Finding #3341]. The link instead runs through the Safra family social network. Edmond Safra's nephew Jacqui Safra appeared on guest lists for Edge Foundation dinners alongside Jeff Bezos, Sergey Brin, and Bill Gates between 2012 and 2014, and was offered as a potential creditor opportunity to Epstein through John Brockman's June 2010 email [Finding #3370]. Ron Soffer worked in banking law at RNB from 1988 to 1991 and later bridged the Safra professional world to the Epstein legal network [Finding #3370]. The bank's significance lies in its historical role as private banking infrastructure and in the family network that persisted after the institution was absorbed by HSBC [Finding #3370].
curation.system_role: Republic National Bank illustrates how a single privately controlled institution served simultaneously as a processing channel for covert government financial flows, a compliance reporter against organized crime, an offshore banking intermediary, and the target of a multi-billion-dollar acquisition — roles made possible by the same cross-border private banking infrastructure.

sections.title: Iran-Contra: Institutional Wire Transfers and the Off-Books Cash Operation
sections.content:
The Walsh Independent Counsel's Iran-Contra Final Report (Volume 1, page 195 and page 221 footnote 20) records Republic National Bank of New York intersecting Enterprise activity through two structurally distinct channels [Finding #3414]. At the institutional level, RNB processed many of the Enterprise's wire transfers through normal banking channels [Finding #3390]. A parallel cash-delivery operation was run by Nan Morabia, an RNB officer who told the FBI in a November 16, 1987 interview that the cash operation "was conducted by her outside bank channels" [Finding #3414]. Nan and her brother David Morabia were granted immunity in exchange for their testimony; a third Morabia sibling, Elliot, died in March 1987 before investigators could interview him [Finding #3414].

The documented cash drops connected RNB's officer-level activity to prominent Iran-Contra figures [Finding #3414]. In August 1985, Nan Morabia delivered $7,000 to Robert Owen at RNB in New York, and on November 26, 1986 she delivered $150,000 in cash to Adnan Khashoggi, who had provided approximately $30 million in bridge financing for US arms sales to Iran [Finding #3414]. Willard Zucker directed the domestic drops from the Swiss side and wired corresponding amounts into a "Codelis" account at Safra's Trade Development Bank in Geneva, controlled by the Mizrahi brothers [Finding #3370]. At least 21 cash transactions totaling approximately $91,000 involving Oliver North alone were structured below the $10,000 Currency Transaction Report threshold [Finding #3414].

Both ends of the Enterprise's US-Swiss cash pipeline ran through institutions controlled by Edmond Safra, with RNB in New York handling wire transfers and TDB Geneva holding the Codelis account [Finding #3370][Finding #3390]. Safra's personal knowledge of the Enterprise's use of his institutions is not established, and the Morabia family's personal cash operation is distinct from RNB's institutional wire-transfer role [Finding #3414]. RNB's precious-metals expertise may have normalized institutional handling of large physical cash volumes, given that the bank had been the first American institution licensed to sell gold for industrial purposes after the 1974 lifting of the private gold ownership ban and was the nation's leading importer of gold coins [Finding #3421].

sections.title: Russian Organized Crime Exposure and the Safra Death Timeline
sections.content:
Contemporaneous reporting and the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations' 2001 Correspondent Banking materials record that in August 1998 RNB's compliance team closed a suspicious Benex Worldwide account and filed Suspicious Activity Reports with the FBI flagging Russian money flows through Bank of New York [Finding #3370]. Benex was linked to Semion Mogilevich, alleged head of a Russian organized crime network; through 18 Benex accounts at Bank of New York approximately $10 billion moved within roughly two years [Finding #3370]. This was a consequential compliance action by a privately controlled US bank against activity at a competitor institution [Finding #3370].

The records assembled on Safra place the events that followed in a tight sequence. Safra had provided approximately $25 million in seed capital to Bill Browder's Hermitage Capital Management in 1996 for Russian investments, giving him direct financial exposure to the same market his bank later reported on [Finding #3370]. Edmond Safra died in a fire at his Monaco penthouse on December 3, 1999, roughly 16 months after the Benex SARs were filed [Finding #3370]. The fire was set by Ted Maher, a nurse and former US Army Green Beret in Safra's employ, who was convicted of arson and manslaughter and who claimed he had intended only a small fire to position himself as a hero [Finding #3370]. The HSBC sale closed on December 31, 1999, 28 days after Safra's death [Finding #3370].

The record establishes a sequence rather than a causal chain [Finding #3370]. RNB exposed a $10 billion Mogilevich-linked operation in August 1998, Safra died in December 1999, and HSBC acquired the Safra banking network 28 days later, transferring approximately 70 offshore entities and six jurisdictions of client relationships into HSBC [Finding #3370]. Whether Russian-state or organized-crime retaliation connects these events is not established [Finding #3370]. The 2001 Levin PSI Correspondent Banking Report cited RNB — by then HSBC USA — as a "notable exception" for adopting a written Know Your Customer Policy Statement for its International Banking Group effective December 31, 1998, adding a compliance dimension to the institutional record during the same window [Finding #3390].

sections.title: Offshore Architecture and Compliance Paradox
sections.content:
OCCRP Aleph and LittleSis records show Republic National Bank of New York operating subsidiaries and related entities across multiple offshore jurisdictions, including Panama and Guernsey [Finding #3414]. RNB-branded structures additionally appeared in Swiss (as Republic National Bank of New York (Suisse) S·A·), Singapore, and Bahamas offshore holdings, documenting a multi-jurisdiction private-banking footprint consistent with the Safra group's Luxembourg and Monaco operations [Finding #3414]. These structures served conventional private-banking and trust functions typical of the period for large international institutions [Finding #3414].

Against this offshore footprint, the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations' 2001 Correspondent Banking report singled out RNB — by then operating as HSBC USA — as a "notable exception" among US banks for having adopted a written Know Your Customer Policy Statement for its International Banking Group, effective December 31, 1998, and requiring written due-diligence analysis for every correspondent-bank applicant [Finding #3390]. Read alongside the Walsh record, the Levin PSI findings suggest the policy may have been adopted in response to lessons from Iran-Contra and from forfeiture exposure rather than as a routine compliance upgrade [Finding #3390].

Taken together, the records describe a two-track compliance profile, pairing an offshore intermediary footprint in at least four jurisdictions with an industry-leading KYC posture on the eve of the HSBC acquisition [Finding #3414][Finding #3390]. The precious-metals business adds relevant context, as the bank's role as America's leading gold coin importer and first institution licensed to sell gold for industrial purposes built in-house expertise for large-volume physical asset handling [Finding #3421]. Offshore intermediary activity alongside public compliance leadership was common among large international private banks of the period and is not by itself indicative of misconduct [Finding #3414].

sections.title: Key Relationships
sections.content:
Nan Morabia was an RNB officer whose role in the Iran-Contra cash operation is the bank's most direct documented connection to covert intelligence-adjacent activity [Finding #3414]. Her cash drops were coordinated by Willard Zucker, who managed the Enterprise's Swiss accounts for Albert Hakim, and were conducted outside official bank channels while using the credentials of an RNB officer [Connection #2020]. Walsh's footnote 20 at page 221 records the Enterprise wire transfers being routed through RNB institutionally, with Zucker managing the Swiss side via CSF Geneva [Connection #2024].

Trade Development Bank (TDB) in Geneva was the institutional sibling to RNB; in the Walsh record both were controlled by Edmond Safra and both appear in the Enterprise fund-flow record [Connection #2029]. RNB's FARA registration as agent for Trade Development Bank Overseas Inc. from September 1975 to June 1976 formalizes the institutional relationship at the primary-source level [FARA:2604]. TDB's Codelis account functioned as the Swiss counterpart to RNB's domestic wire processing, a pairing the Walsh record presents as effectively a single operational channel for Enterprise fund flows [Finding #3370][Connection #2029].

Adnan Khashoggi was the most prominent named recipient of RNB officer-level cash flows, receiving $150,000 from Nan Morabia on November 26, 1986 [Finding #3414]. Khashoggi had provided approximately $30 million in bridge financing for the Iran arms sales, which positions the Morabia delivery as the RNB network's most direct documented intersection with the Enterprise's principal private financier [Finding #3414].

The Epstein-network link flows through Jacqui Safra, Edmond's nephew, a documented presence at Edge Foundation dinners alongside Jeffrey Epstein, Jeff Bezos, Sergey Brin, and Bill Gates between 2012 and 2014 [Finding #3370]. John Brockman's June 2010 email to Epstein reported Jacqui's banking difficulties and asked "Something for you??", establishing Epstein as a potential creditor to Safra family members while Jacqui attempted to sell Epstein his Jerusalem property, which had previously been in negotiations with Ronald Lauder [Finding #3370]. Ron Soffer worked in banking law at RNB from 1988 to 1991 and later became a figure in the Epstein legal network, bridging the Safra professional world to the Epstein orbit through legal rather than banking channels [Finding #3370].

sections.title: Legal and Regulatory Proceedings
sections.content:
The CourtListener docket records a federal forfeiture case, United States v. Republic National Bank (1:90-cv-00613, EDNY), filed February 21, 1990, and terminated April 30, 1993, under nature-of-suit code 690 (Other forfeiture and penalty suits), assigned to Judge Raymond Joseph Dearie with Magistrate Allyne R. Ross. The three-year contested proceeding saw RNB dispute a government asset seizure. No formal link between this action and the Enterprise's use of RNB has been established, though the case was filed roughly three years after the Iran-Contra cash drops Walsh later documented [Finding #3414].

A separate criminal matter preceded and reduced the HSBC acquisition price from $10.3 billion to $9.85 billion. During the pendency of the HSBC acquisition announced in May 1999, RNB was convicted in a scheme to defraud Japanese investors and paid fines exceeding $600 million [Finding #3414]. RNB filed FARA Registration #2604 from its 452 Fifth Avenue address in New York between September 4, 1975 and June 10, 1976 on behalf of Trade Development Bank (Overseas) Incorporated in the Philippines. That filing provides primary-source confirmation of the institutional relationship between RNB and TDB Geneva and documents the bank's formal role as a registered agent for Safra's offshore banking interests within the US regulatory framework [FARA:2604][Finding #3414].

open_questions: What was the substance of the 1990 federal forfeiture case (US v. Republic National Bank, 1:90-cv-00613 EDNY)? What assets were seized and what underlying criminal activity did the government allege, and does the three-year timeline connect to the Walsh Iran-Contra investigation's parallel proceedings?

Did Edmond Safra have personal knowledge of the Enterprise's use of both RNB (New York) and TDB (Geneva) for covert fund flows, or were the Morabia cash operations and the Codelis account exploitations of access by intelligence-adjacent actors working through an officer of the bank?

What was the relationship, if any, between RNB's August 1998 reporting of the Bank of New York / Benex / Mogilevich activity and Safra's death in December 1999? Were there documented threats, surveillance operations, or retaliation linked to the exposure of the $10 billion laundering scheme?

Who were the Munbank Trust beneficiaries behind the RNB Guernsey trustee structure identified in the Panama Papers (ICIJ node 12200780), and what is the provenance of the assets held in that structure?

How much of HSBC's subsequent AML failures — culminating in the 2012 $1.9 billion settlement for anti-money-laundering control failures — traces to infrastructure, client relationships, or compliance gaps inherited from the Safra network acquired in December 1999?

What was the nature of Ron Soffer's work at RNB from 1988 to 1991, and did it overlap with the period of the federal forfeiture case or the American Express defamation campaign against Safra? What specific clients or matters did Soffer handle during his time at the bank?

The ACRIS database returns 100+ NYC property records for Republic National Bank. Do any of these transactions connect to properties associated with Epstein-linked entities, Safra family holdings, or Iran-Contra network figures?
